initial_assumptions: Intronic variant in Lynch gene is likely pathogenic via exon 5 skipping
Clinically observed in 3 colorectal cancer patients
constraints: Exon skipping must be proven by minigene or RNA

evidence_schedule.content: InSiGHT VCEP requirement: +3A>T variants cannot take PVS1 without patient-derived RNA showing complete out-of-frame transcript loss.
Three reported colorectal cancer families carrying c.942+3A>T also carry a co-occurring pathogenic MLH1 stop-gain mutation.
CRITICAL REVERSAL: High-throughput mini-gene assay and blood RNA assay demonstrate 100% normal splicing; no aberrant transcript produced. Invalidates splicing pathogenicity assumption!
gnomAD non-cancer cohort reveals frequency 0.006 (0.6%), exceeding Lynch syndrome maximum credible frequency (BS1).

ground_truth.provenance: Historical reclassification from VUS/Likely Pathogenic to Likely Benign by InSiGHT panel.
